Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to pull together the pricing and SLA options so we can evaluate cost for a Q3 pilot (expected ~150M tokens/month). Two specific asks from our side:

- Can you confirm uptime tiers you offer and what the effective credit is for downtime? We need the 24/7 availability and clear remedial credits for procurement.
- For premium support, what are your P1/P2 response times and whether that includes on-call escalation to engineering?

Also, Acme is evaluating a one-time onboarding discount for the pilot. What flexibility do you have on a short-term discount (6–12 months) vs committed longer-term pricing?

If you can share a short price/SLA matrix and any draft SOW we can circulate internally, that would be ideal.

Best,
Lisa

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short matrix and a draft SOW (see Redwood_SLA_Pricing_20260520.pdf and Draft_SOW_Acme_20260520.docx). Below is a concise summary of the options and what we can offer for a pilot.

---- SLA & Support packages (summary) ----
1) Standard Support (included)
   - Uptime target: 99.90% monthly
   - Response: Business hours support, next-business-day triage for incidents
   - Credits: standard SLA credits per contract (up to 10% monthly cap)

2) Enhanced Availability (recommended for pilot)
   - Uptime target: 99.95% monthly
   - Response: 24/7 triage; P1 initial response within 1 hour; P2 within 4 hours
   - Escalation: Access to on-call SRE + weekly sync during onboarding window
   - Credits: enhanced credit schedule (outlined in attached PDF)

3) Premium (enterprise SLA)
   - Uptime target: 99.99% with guaranteed remediation SLAs
   - Response: 24/7 dedicated escalation channel, on-site support options (where applicable)

Pricing notes:
- Support is an add-on priced as a percentage of committed capacity. For the pilot (~150M tokens/month) we price Enhanced Availability at a blended rate. Full details in the attachment.
- We can consider a short-term onboarding discount. Typical approvals: sales leadership + finance sign-off.

If you are evaluating a 6-month pilot, an internal path we commonly use is a limited-duration discount (pilot pricing) with a commitment to revisit at renewal — and we often tie deeper discounts to multi-quarter committed capacity.

Next steps:
- I can propose a pilot offer if you share whether Acme prefers a 6- or 12-month pilot and any minimum committed spend.
- Marissa (cc’d) will help with the SOW details and onboarding checkpoints.

Thanks — I’ll assemble a formal pilot offer once I hear your preference.

Best,

Subject: Fwd: Redwood SLA/pricing details for pilot evaluation — quick approval request

Team — forwarding Acme’s ask and my summary (below). Acme is evaluating a 6 vs 12 month pilot, ~150M tokens/month. They requested an onboarding discount.

Proposed commercial ask from me: 25% off support add-on for first 12 months, or 30% off if they commit to a 12-month reserved capacity plan. Also proposing to limit SLA credits for pilot to a 10% monthly cap and require a 6-week ramp before premium credits apply.

Could you confirm approvals needed? Finance has historically pushed back on >20% for pilot discounts without reorder commitments. If we proceed with 25% I’ll need sales leadership + finance alignment and a legal clause limiting credits for pilot term.

Quoted original message:
> Lisa: Procurement asked me to pull together the pricing and SLA options so we can evaluate cost for a Q3 pilot...

Thanks — Neha

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood SLA/pricing details for pilot evaluation — quick approval request

Neha —

I discussed with finance. We can approve a concession for a pilot but within guardrails:
- Approve: 20% off the Enhanced Availability support add-on for the first 6 months (pilot period).
- Condition: Acme signs a 6-month committed pilot SOW and agrees to a follow-on commercial review 30 days before pilot end.
- SLA credit cap: keep the 10% monthly cap. No retrospective increase in credits for pilot term.
- Legal: include a clause that any deeper discount for renewal requires executive approval and a signed reorder.

Rationale: preserves runway and limits exposure while making the price attractive for evaluation. If Acme does a 12-month committed reserved capacity, we can consider phasing to 25% through the contract negotiation.

Markus
Markus Klein | Head of Sales Operations
markus_klein@redwood.ai
